_comment: Reviewed hazards for atlas reference pages (#4460). Each entry applies to the type and its subtypes unless a subtype has its own entry. Every evidence string must still appear in its source file; tests/atlas_habitats checks this, so a changed mechanic fails until the entry is reviewed again.

hazards.hazard: Burns the legs of anyone who steps in; fresh lava can burn a foot or leg off.
Too deep to stand in. Swimming tires you out in under a minute, faster in a storm, and then you go under. A lifejacket or a sealed diving suit keeps you afloat. Things dropped here sink.
evidence:
A lifejacket
// or a sealed diving suit floats its wearer

hazards.hazard: There is no air down here: you need a sealed diving suit with an air bottle. Each suit is only rated for some depths, and deeper water crushes it.
evidence: The sea crushes \the [S] in and water floods your helmet!

hazards.hazard: Nothing to stand on: anyone who steps in falls to the level below and is hurt by the landing, unless something covers the hole.
evidence: falls from the level above and slams into the floor!

hazards.hazard: Cuts the feet and legs of anyone who walks through it.
While lit, it burns the legs of anyone who walks through it.
Once set, its steel jaws bite whoever steps on it and hold them in place.
Once set, it badly wounds the legs of whoever falls in and holds them there.
evidence: You fall into the punji sticks trap, and are stuck!

hazards.hazard: Its bite is venomous and poisons the leg it strikes.
Wraps around whoever it attacks and holds them still until it is killed or lets go.
Swarms toward people and bites; a bite can pass on malaria. Rain drives them off.
Its threads burn any diver who touches it or swims beside it. A hard diving suit is too thick for them.
Waits in a rock crevice and bites divers who swim close.
evidence: waits in a crevice and snaps at whatever swims too close
